Answer: A
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates a well-circumscribed, rounded opacity in the middle mediastinum that causes anterior bowing (displacement) of the trachea. This specific location and mass effect on the airway are classic radiographic features of a bronchogenic cyst, whereas lymphomas typically present as lobulated masses without such smooth displacement, and thymic lesions are located anteriorly.
